request.spec:
Each user has a locale (a select on the screen, en unless chosen, saved per user, no audit line).
Under de, every figure the screen shows that user (amounts, due figures, totals, rates, shares,
cuts: any cell whose whole text is a number with two decimals) is shown as 1.234,56 (a dot every
three digits, a comma before the decimals); under en as before. Entries are typed with a dot as
before, and exports and audit lines are unchanged.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user has a locale (a select on the screen, en unless chosen, saved per user, no audit line).
Under de, every figure the screen shows that user (amounts, due figures, totals, rates, shares,
cuts: any cell whose whole text is a number with two decimals) is shown as 1.234,56 (a dot every
three digits, a comma before the decimals); under en as before. Entries are typed with a dot as
before, and exports and audit lines are unchanged.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The locale feature works and the main locale test passes. Overall 3 of the 4 tests in the spec pass. The failing one, scenario 2, fails on a plans check that my change doesn't touch.

**Test results (`bin/e2e`)**
- ✓ `user locale`: under `de` uma sees `9.999,99`, `1.234.565,77`, `10,00`, `0,00` and so on. vic sees the same sheet in `en` at the same time. After uma switches back to `en`, everything shows the old way. The CSV export and audit lines are unchanged.
- ✓ scenarios 1 and 3.
- ✘ scenario 2, line 678: `expect(await ui.generatePlans(pg_wes)).toBe(0)`. `wes` is a viewer at that point. The server refuses any change by a viewer, including generating plan claims (`ValidatePlanGenerate` → `RoleStore.refuseChange`). That refusal is also written down in `plans/generate.POST.yml`. So the screen shows the error and the test expects a count of `0`. To check the rest of the scenario, I ran a temporary copy of the spec with only that assertion relaxed (since deleted). Everything else in scenario 2 passed. I didn't change the viewer rule because it's outside this request and is documented behaviour. If the spec is right, the fix would be to let a viewer's generate that would make nothing answer `0` — say if you want that.

**Server**
- New table `user_locale` (`V72__user_locale.sql`). It holds one locale per user per sheet, and `en` is the default when there's no row. I keyed it by sheet because AGENTS.md says everything is kept per sheet, and so tests that share user names don't interfere with each other.
- `GET` and `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/locale`, under `app/locale/`. They write no audit line. Any locale other than `en` or `de`, or a missing user, is refused with a 400.
- `AsOfGuard` now lets `/locale` requests through: a locale changes only how one user's screen looks, not the sheet, so it isn't blocked while the screen shows the sheet as of a date.

**Front end**
- `features/locale/locale.ts` loads the user's locale and has `formatFigure`/`useFigure()`. Under `de`, any text that is wholly a number with two decimals becomes `1.234,56`; everything else is left as it is.
- `features/locale/locale.slot.tsx` adds the header control: `user-locale`, `user-locale-save`, `user-locale-current`, and `user-locale-error` for a refusal.
- I applied `fig(...)` to every cell that shows a figure across 22 slot files: amounts, due totals, rollups, header and consolidated totals, rates, cuts, shares, aged buckets, periods, tags, months, the rate-preview difference, plan amounts, and the money/percent setting values. Input boxes, CSV exports and audit lines are untouched, so entries are still typed with a dot.
